findings.title: restore-check spawn tests have no timeout though each spawns node + supabase-js
findings.evidence: restoreCheck() spawnSync(process.execPath, [scripts/restore-check.mjs ...]) in 7 tests at lines 51-85 with the default 5 s timeout; scripts/restore-check.mjs:31 imports @supabase/supabase-js at module load, before argv parsing (line 49). Baseline test.log: 5 of them timed out at 5.7-9.3 s.
findings.proposed_fix: Give the describe blocks at lines 50 and 59 a 30_000 timeout like the one at line 86 (or set testTimeout for the file); optionally lazy-import createClient in scripts/restore-check.mjs after argument parsing so --help exits in ~100 ms.
findings.impact: pnpm test exits 1 on a loaded machine (yesterday baseline), blocking pnpm check and acceptance for a reason unrelated to the code; the same tests pass when idle. Fault: the test (no timeout on a process-spawning test, unlike the 30_000 given to the --extract failures describe), compounded by the script loading supabase-js before it parses --help.

findings.title: pdf.js real-preview test timeout (15 s) too tight for the parallel unit pool
findings.evidence: it(..., 15_000) imports pdfjs-dist/legacy and parses public/book/khous-preview.pdf (356 KB); baseline test.log: 27442 ms, "Test timed out in 15000ms".
findings.proposed_fix: Raise the timeout to 60_000, or move this one test to tests/integration (it is a fixture-file check, not a unit).
findings.impact: pnpm test exits 1 under load, same as TEST-UNIT-01; the code under test (fixLigatures) is not at fault, the import of pdf.js inside a contended fork is.

findings.title: riyadhLocalToIsoOrNull accepts an impossible day (Feb 30) and the test never tries one
findings.evidence: node: new Date("2026-02-30T10:00:00+03:00").toISOString() -> 2026-03-02T07:00:00.000Z. src/lib/money-input.ts:63-67 only regex-checks the shape then trusts Date; the test lists month 13 and five-digit years but no day overflow.
findings.proposed_fix: In riyadhLocalToIsoOrNull, after parsing, compare new Date(time).toISOString().slice(0,16) shifted back by 3 h with the input (or reuse isDay on the date part); add expect(riyadhLocalToIsoOrNull("2026-02-30T10:00")).toBeNull() to the test.
findings.impact: A coupon or schedule datetime typed as 2026-02-30 is silently stored as 2 March; the sibling isDay() in src/lib/admin-commerce.ts:60 already documents that 2026-02-30 is not a day, so the two helpers disagree.

findings.title: isHostedSite, the guard behind the Turnstile test-secret refusal and real email, has no unit test
findings.evidence: env.test.ts covers isLocalDatabaseUrl, assertLocalTestDatabase, secretsMatch, requireEnv; nothing imports isHostedSite or optionalEnv. supabase/functions/_shared/env.ts:65-73: unset or unparsable SITE_URL -> false (treated as local).
findings.proposed_fix: Add a describe for isHostedSite: https://anas.studio -> true; http://localhost:3000, http://127.0.0.1:54321, http://host.docker.internal -> false; unset -> false; "not a url" -> false. Record the fail-open semantics for Turnstile in the deployment checklist (SITE_URL is required).
findings.impact: A mutation that inverts the LOCAL_HOSTS test or drops the try/catch passes the suite; turnstile.test.ts only proves the composite with SITE_URL set. Unset SITE_URL on a deployed function means a configured test secret passes every form (turnstile.ts:69); email and Moyasar fail safe in that case, Turnstile does not.

findings.title: clientKeyHash: pepper and UTC-date salt are asserted by no test
findings.evidence: The only clientKeyHash test compares two hashes made with the same pepper on the same day. rate-limit.ts:62 material = `${pepper}:${utcDate}:${throttleAddress(ip)}`; deleting pepper or utcDate from the template leaves every assertion green.
findings.proposed_fix: Add: a hash with pepper "b" differs from pepper "a" for the same request; with vi.useFakeTimers set to 2026-10-05T23:59:59Z vs 2026-10-06T00:00:01Z the same request hashes differently; and the hash is 64 lower-case hex.
findings.impact: The privacy property DATA-AND-SECURITY relies on (the stored key cannot be correlated across days or reversed without the pepper) is not protected by the suite; the rate limit itself would still work, so nothing else would notice.

findings.title: staffFromRequest: the inactive-row, unknown-role, lookup-error and non-Bearer branches have no unit test
findings.evidence: The only positive case stubs maybeSingle() to {role: owner, active: true}. staff.ts:47 role = staff.data?.active && ROLES.has(role) ? role : null; staff.ts:46 throws STAFF_LOOKUP_FAILED; staff.ts:34 non-Bearer -> null. None of those branches is driven by a unit test; every admin-*.test.ts fakes the resolver.
findings.proposed_fix: Add to the describe at line 33: active:false -> role null; role "superuser" -> role null; maybeSingle error -> rejects STAFF_LOOKUP_FAILED; header "Basic x" and no header -> null; claims without sub -> null.
findings.impact: A one-line mutation that drops `staff.data?.active &&` (D13: a revoked member loses access on the next call) passes the whole unit suite; only tests/integration/disputes-http.test.ts:196-201 would notice, and only for an action whose SQL rechecks the actor. Unit tests of the admin handlers suggest authorization is covered, but what they cover is the gate given a trusted identity.

findings.title: verifyTurnstile: the outgoing siteverify request (URL, body keys, remoteip omission) is never asserted
findings.evidence: Every test stubs fetch with vi.fn(async () => Response) and asserts only the mapped result; no test reads fetch.mock.calls. turnstile.ts:76-85 builds the URL, {secret, response, remoteip} and the 5 s AbortSignal.
findings.proposed_fix: In the success test, capture the stub and assert fetch was called once with SITEVERIFY_URL, method POST, JSON body {secret, response: "tok", remoteip: "203.0.113.7"}; add a case with remoteIp "local" asserting no remoteip key.
findings.impact: Swapping the body keys (secret <-> response), a typo in SITEVERIFY_URL, or sending remoteip "local" would leave every unit test green; checkout.test.ts:867 asserts only what the handler hands the injected verifier, not what the verifier sends. The e2e run with the test secret is the only check, and it does not inspect the request either.

findings.title: content.test.ts drift check is a conditional it.skip that never runs in CI, so the verbatim-text invariant is machine-dependent
findings.evidence: if (!existsSync(CONTENT_MD)) { it.skip(...); return } — the source is git-excluded; on CI and on any machine without BOOK_ASSETS the four verbatim assertions do not run.
findings.proposed_fix: Store a sha256 of the normalized CONTENT.md excerpts in the repo (no text) and compare against the JSON fields, so CI can run the check without the asset.
findings.impact: A change to content/initial-content.json that alters Anas's text passes CI; only the owner's machine would see it. Recorded by the test itself; no new defect.
